title: Designing a 60 ft Loaded 80 m Dipole with loadedDipole
text: section sweep coil position compute required inductance position, evaluate efficiency. gives realistic view coil placement affects performance.  sweep computes: actual required inductance B corresponding coil loss effect shortening radiation resistance thus true efficiency curve
code: library(ggplot2)  wire_diameter = 0.065  # sweep from 10% to 90% of half-length half_len <- total_length / 2 fractions <- seq(0.01, 0.99, by = 0.01) coil_positions <- fractions * half_len  eff_list <- lapply(seq_along(coil_positions), function(i) {   B <- coil_positions[i]    # compute required inductance at this coil position   L_req <- loading_coil_inductance(     frequency,     total_length = total_length,     coil_position = B,     wire_diameter = wire_diameter,     metric = FALSE   )    # compute efficiency using segmented model   eff <- estimate_efficiency(     frequency       = frequency,     total_length    = total_length,     coil_inductance = L_req,     coil_position   = B,     model           = "segmented"   )    data.frame(     coil_position = B,     fraction_of_half = fractions[i],     inductance = L_req,     efficiency = -10 * log10(eff$efficiency)    ) })  eff_df <- do.call(rbind, eff_list)  # plot the result ggplot(eff_df, aes(x = coil_position, y = efficiency)) +   geom_line(size = 1.1) +   geom_vline(     xintercept = rec$coil_position,     linetype = "dashed",     color = "red"   ) +   annotate(     "text",     x = rec$coil_position,     y = max(eff_df$efficiency),     label = sprintf("Recommended: %.2f ft", rec$coil_position),     vjust = -0.5,     color = "red"   ) +   labs(     x = "Coil position from feedpoint (ft)",     y = "Efficiency",     title = "Efficiency vs Coil Position (Required Inductance Computed per Position)",     subtitle = "Dashed line shows recommended coil placement"   ) +   theme_minimal() ## Warning: Using `size` aesthetic for lines was deprecated in ggplot2 3.4.0. ## ℹ Please use `linewidth` instead. ## This warning is displayed once every 8 hours. ## Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was ## generated.

title: Designing a 60 ft Loaded 80 m Dipole with loadedDipole
text: common design question : “move coils inward, can use smaller inductance without hurting efficiency?” optimize_inductance_for_position() allows us sweep coil placements, compute required inductance, optionally compute efficiency. analyze 60 ft 80-meter dipole 3.57 MHz: can now visualize inductance efficiency vary coil placement:   demonstrates : Moving coils inward reduces required inductance dramatically Efficiency stays nearly flat, expected short 80-meter dipole Practical positions (≈10–15 ft feedpoint) allow much smaller, lower-loss coils without meaningful loss radiated power

what: Designing a loaded dipole when only the total length is known
title: Designing a 60 ft Loaded 80 m Dipole with loadedDipole
text: Often builder knows available span (e.g., 60 ft) wishes design rest antenna constraint loading coils must exceed value. solve problem 60 ft dipole 3.57 MHz, allowing coils 66 µH. output gives recommended coil placement inductance : Requires 66 µH, within 0.1 dB best achievable efficiency, Uses smallest inductance within range. can also visualize entire design space:
code: library(loadedDipole)  design <- design_loaded_dipole(   frequency    = 3.57,   total_length = 60,   L_max        = 66 )  design$best ##   coil_position inductance efficiency   loss_dB ## 1             8   33.56123  0.9670797 0.1453773 library(ggplot2)  df <- design$designs  ggplot(df, aes(x = coil_position, y = inductance)) +   geom_line(color="steelblue", size=1) +   geom_point(data = design$best, aes(x = coil_position, y = inductance),              color="red", size=3) +   labs(     title = "Required inductance vs coil position (60 ft dipole, 3.57 MHz)",     x = "Coil position (ft from feedpoint)",     y = "Inductance (µH)"   ) ggplot(df, aes(x = coil_position, y = loss_dB)) +   geom_line(size=1) +   geom_point(data = design$best, aes(x = coil_position, y = loss_dB),              color="red", size=3) +   labs(     title = "Efficiency loss vs coil position (segmented model)",     x = "Coil position (ft)",     y = "Loss relative to perfect dipole (dB)"   )

text: function implements Jerry Hall (QST Sep 1974) formula inductance loading coil used shorten half‑wave dipole antenna. returns inductance coil micro‑henries given operating frequency, total physical length dipole, distance feedpoint coil, conductor diameter.  formula relies logarithmic terms defined distances measured imperial units (feet inches).  `metric = TRUE` inputs converted metres (lengths) metres (wire diameter) feet inches internally.  details equation variable definitions see Hall's article subsequent summaries【584486973026570†L36-L68】.

Two coils assumed symmetrically placed side feedpoint. wire_diameter Diameter dipole conductor.  `metric` `TRUE` metres; otherwise inches.  unspecified default 0.065 inches (approx. what: Recommend a loading-coil placement for a given dipole and inductance — recommend_coil_position
title: Recommend a loading-coil placement for a given dipole and inductance — recommend_coil_position
text: helper solves distance feedpoint loading coil (per leg) yields specified coil inductance desired operating frequency total dipole length. calculation inverts loading_coil_inductance() relation using numerical root finding coil position. Results based Jerry Hall short-dipole model therefore assume two identical coils placed symmetrically leg centre-fed dipole.

title: Recommend a loading-coil placement for a given dipole and inductance — recommend_coil_position
text: frequency Operating frequency megahertz (MHz). total_length Total physical length dipole. Feet metric = FALSE, metres otherwise. inductance Target loading-coil inductance (per coil) microhenries (uH). wire_diameter Diameter dipole conductor. Defaults 0.065 inches (approximately AWG 14) metric = FALSE; supply metres metric = TRUE. metric Logical; TRUE, length quantities interpreted metres converted internally imperial units. FALSE, lengths assumed feet diameters inches. target_fraction Optional numeric value 0 1 giving preferred fraction half-length coil position (0 = feedpoint, 1 = end leg). supplied search solution biased around fraction; NULL broad search 10–90% half-length used.

what: Solve for an unknown loaded dipole parameter — solve_loaded_dipole
title: Solve for an unknown loaded dipole parameter — solve_loaded_dipole
text: Given two operating frequency, required loading coil inductance total physical length dipole, function solves remaining parameter determines optimum coil placement.  `frequency` `total_length` supplied minimises coil inductance respect coil position.  `frequency` `inductance` supplied searches total length yields specified inductance optimum coil position.  `total_length` `inductance` supplied searches frequency satisfies inductance optimum coil position.  calculations use Jerry Hall formula coil inductance【584486973026570†L36-L68】.

title: Solve for an unknown loaded dipole parameter — solve_loaded_dipole
code: solve_loaded_dipole(   frequency = NA,   inductance = NA,   total_length = NA,   wire_diameter = 0.065,   metric = FALSE,   search_length_range = NULL,   search_frequency_range = NULL )

title: Solve for an unknown loaded dipole parameter — solve_loaded_dipole
text: frequency Operating frequency megahertz (MHz).  Use `NA` unknown parameter. inductance Coil inductance per loading coil microhenries (uH). Use `NA` unknown parameter. total_length Total physical length dipole feet (metres `metric = TRUE`).  Use `NA` unknown parameter. wire_diameter Diameter dipole conductor.  default 0.065 inches corresponds AWG 14.  metric units specify metres. metric Logical; `TRUE` length inputs/outputs metres (wire diameter metres).  `FALSE` (default) feet inches used. search_length_range Optional numeric vector length two giving lower upper limits total length searching solution. `NULL` total length unknown, function uses range 0.2 × (full‑size dipole length) full‑size dipole length (`468/frequency`).  search units `total_length`. search_frequency_range Optional numeric vector length two giving lower upper limits frequency searching solution (MHz). `NULL` frequency unknown, range c(0.5, 30) MHz.

title: Solve for an unknown loaded dipole parameter — solve_loaded_dipole
